newsitem.title: USA: Gold rebounds but analysts see renewed weakness.
newsitem.headline: Gold rebounds but analysts see renewed weakness.

text.p: Gold rebounded Tuesday as bargain hunters resurfaced after the precious metal lost nearly $15 an ounce since last Thursday, but some analysts said the metal was still trapped in a downtrend, and they forecast the price could slip to $300 within three months.
In early morning trading, August gold was up $3.20 at $322.20 an ounce on New York's Commodity Exchange, rallying from Monday's $319.00 an ounce, a level unseen since 1985.
In London, gold was fixed at $317.60, down from $318.00 Monday afternoon and far below its $334.00 price a week ago.
"These markets have been going sideways for so long that now that a trend has started it will be very significant," said Fran Skelley, an analyst for Credit Suisse First Boston.
Dealers said the market was still very soft amid signs that further losses were in store.

Gold, which has been under pressure all year from central bank selling of gold reserves, finally cracked last Thursday when the Reserve Bank of Australia announced it had sold 167 tons of gold during the last six months.
The shockwaves from that were amplified by the fact that Australia is the world's third-largest gold producer.
"If ever a move could have been calculated to extinguish what flickering flame of investor hope remained, then this was it," said Nick Moore, an analyst for Flemings Global Mining Group.
Market sentiment was the most negative in years for gold.

Aside from the constant threat of fresh central bank selling, there was a growing view that investors really had no valid reason to get involved with the yellow metal as a long-term way of making money.
Dealers say the metal could test its 1985 low of $287.25 on fears that other central banks might unload some of their 35,000 tons of gold that are held by government institutions around the globe.
Gold sank in 1985 in tandem with a collapse in the price of oil.
